panels.body: Private authorized order and billing evidence; no invented paid status or automatic processor integration.

note: SaaS subscription fees do not become customer Snowflake charges.

title: Help & support
description: Resolve issues with safe, useful context.

panels.title: Support request
panels.body: Issue category, concise description, affected time/scope and sanitized support bundle preview.

panels.title: Support access
panels.body: Time-bounded audited authorization; no standing cross-tenant access or raw credential collection.

note: Mockup stores a local request draft and contacts nobody.

title: Welcome to Bridge
description: Your Snowflake cost, with clarity and control.

panels.title: Sign-in card
panels.body: Workspace domain → Continue with SSO. Production redirects to Cognito with validated state/PKCE and exact redirect URIs.

panels.title: Privacy
panels.body: Do not put tokens in local storage or URLs. The prototype uses no real identity provider.

note: No passwords, MFA codes or tokens should be entered in this public synthetic mockup.

title: Verify your sign-in
description: A step-up check before sensitive access.

panels.title: MFA handoff
panels.body: Real MFA challenge is managed by identity provider. Do not create a fake six-digit secret collection form.

panels.title: Recovery
panels.body: Use approved recovery flow, with rate limits and audited admin support.

note: Prototype Continue is navigation only, never proof of authentication.

title: Stored procedures
description: Separate parent invocation from attributed child queries.

panels.title: Call hierarchy
panels.body: Parent procedure and child query links require verified IDs; do not infer exact call structure from similar SQL.

panels.title: Cost accounting
panels.body: Charge each query once, then attribute it to the procedure when evidence permits. Parent runtime and summed child runtime differ.

note: The unobserved sample procedure has no synthetic billed amount. Query compute KPI is broader account context and labelled as such.

title: Dynamic tables
description: Refresh cost and freshness objectives together.

panels.title: Refresh history
panels.body: Refresh mode, timestamps, rows, warehouse and status are evidence fields; missing cost attribution remains null.

panels.title: SLA investigation
panels.body: A missed freshness target is distinct from missing refresh telemetry. Link source coverage before calling it a failed refresh.

note: No fabricated cost or exact refresh count when refresh history is unavailable.

title: Native Applications
description: Provider fees and execution costs as distinct components.

panels.title: Cost layers
panels.body: The 1,000 USD application fee is already in the ledger. Compute may belong to warehouse/SPCS parents; do not add allocated compute twice.

panels.title: Ownership
panels.body: Verified installation/application IDs map to external ownership. Provider identities and contracts are permission scoped.

note: Application fee is observed; execution linkage is unavailable in the fixture.

title: Custom applications
description: Verified application identity before cost attribution.

panels.title: Classification
panels.body: Explicit application metadata outranks weak query-type heuristics. Conflicting evidence stays unresolved.

panels.title: Journey
panels.body: Application → environment → activity → query. Show unavailable child levels when IDs are missing.

note: Do not invent application cost by subtracting unrelated known categories.

title: Ad hoc activity
description: Make unclassified usage inspectable without exposing query secrets.

panels.title: Unknown ownership
panels.body: Unknown classification is a valid bucket, not a default assignment to a guessed user or team.

panels.title: Investigation
panels.body: Authorized query hashes, sanitized text and role metadata support manual review. Group-restricted viewers receive only their scope.

note: This unavailable fixture is not evidence of zero ad hoc cost; the two known query groups cover the observed compute example.

title: Execution explorer
description: A full query-column contract with safe synthetic examples.

panels.title: Column chooser
panels.body: Default subset favors query ID, compute, duration, warehouse and workload; all 16 fields are discoverable through column selection and horizontal scroll.

panels.title: Cost basis
panels.body: Representative query uses 1.40 attributed compute credits at fixture rate 2 USD/credit; query cost is a component, not a second billed charge.

note: One representative execution, not a full export of the 12,480-query month. Parameterized hash version is h_fin_v1; literal text remains sanitized.

title: Warehouse performance
description: Queue, utilization and failures qualified by observation coverage.

panels.title: Capacity context
panels.body: Warehouse type, size, cluster policy, queue time and spill must be read together; a high cost alone does not prove oversizing.

panels.title: People and applications
panels.body: Known service aliases are query metadata, not proof of human ownership. Business tags remain the ownership layer.

note: Utilization unavailable is never zero. Resource modifications require a separately approved action.

title: Cortex Search
description: Service cost and freshness without token assumptions.

panels.title: Native usage
panels.body: Expose indexing/serving units only when present in the verified source contract. Do not borrow AI-function token formulas.

panels.title: Attribution
panels.body: 150 USD is inside the 600 USD Cortex family total. Application attribution may be unknown.

note: No token estimate or guessed price is shown.

title: Cortex Analyst
description: Request activity with the native billing basis.

panels.title: Cost authority
panels.body: 50 USD belongs inside the 600 USD family total; exact source/service model determines supported native units.

panels.title: Privacy
panels.body: Semantic request labels can be shown after sanitization; user questions and generated SQL remain protected.

note: Request count unavailable; do not divide by an invented denominator.

title: forecast_api service
description: Service allocation within pool_analytics

panels.title: Resource context
panels.body: Service runtime and node telemetry support the chosen allocation method; pool total remains authoritative.

panels.title: Shared capacity
panels.body: 500 / 800 = 62.5% of the pool under this published allocation version. A different policy is a new version.

note: Pool plus service rows do not sum to 1,600 USD.

title: Organizations & accounts
description: Discover accounts and make capability boundaries explicit.

panels.title: Discovery review
panels.body: Show discovered, connected, excluded and unreachable accounts separately. An account omitted by privileges cannot be claimed nonexistent.

panels.title: Safe refresh
panels.body: Account discovery is repeatable and records verification time/capabilities. It never creates customer-specific pipeline code.

note: One observed synthetic account does not claim complete coverage of an actual organization.

title: Roles & access scopes
description: Explicit permissions with group and account boundaries.

panels.title: Role editor
panels.body: Choose named capabilities, allowed scopes, effective membership and audited reason. Cannot grant broader scope than actor may delegate.

panels.title: Isolation preview
panels.body: Client role preview is UX only. Production API and Snowflake/PostgreSQL policies independently reject guessed cross-tenant identifiers.

note: No frontend role switch is represented as real security enforcement.
